symptom: `alter page … { set (Action: call microflow M.F) on card1; }` on a container created with `Action:` fails at check and exec: widget "card1" (Forms$DivContainer) has no Action property — Action can only be set on a widget that performs an on-click action, such as a button or a clickable container. `set (OnClick: …)` / `set (OnClickAction: …)` point back to `set (Action: …)`
cause: SetWidgetAction only accepted a widget holding an `Action` key. The metamodel spells the click action per type: Action (buttons, navigation list items), OnClickAction (Forms$DivContainer), ClickAction (Forms$ListView, Forms$StaticImageViewer, Forms$DynamicImageViewer). The refusal's unit test used a DivContainer fixture with no OnClickAction — a shape no stored model holds — so it pinned the bug as the guard
file: `mdl/backend/pagemutator/mutator.go` (SetWidgetAction, clickActionKey); `mdl/types/widget_click_action.go` (WidgetClickActionKeys, shared with the catalog's primary-action reader)
insight: The catalog already knew the three keys (`widgetActionKeys` in mdl/catalog/builder_pages.go) while the mutator knew one: a second reader of the same model fact, the duplicate-resolver shape. Grep the gen package for every `NewPart("…Action")` to get the real list rather than trusting either copy: no type declares two of them, so the first key the stored widget holds is its click action. Check the fixture before trusting a refusal test — a fixture missing a required property can make a wrong refusal look like a guard. The cheapest proof the write matches CREATE is a re-exec of the describe output reporting `Unchanged page`; `mx check --no-update-widgets` gives 0 errors on 11.12.5, for a container that had an action and for one that had none
